primaryFinding: The 95 general-consensus losses were not explained by one dominant opponent feature. Instead, losses were associated with a broader accumulation of opponent-oriented pregame threat plus lower V16/V68 conviction. The equal-weight all-signal threat index separated losses from wins more clearly than any single directional feature within this route.

singleSignalConclusion.interpretation: Within the general V16+V68 consensus route, no single one of the 16 frozen directional opponent-warning signals survived the complete multiple-testing/effect-size/AUC/all-season criterion. This differs from V72's pooled-route result and means the 95-loss mechanism is multidimensional rather than reducible to lineup exposure alone.

allSignalThreatIndex.definition: Equal-weight percentile-rank average of all available frozen opponent-warning signals; no fitted/outcome weights.

strongestDomain.interpretationBoundary: This five-domain family was descriptive and not Holm-corrected across domains, so this is a strong contextual result, not a promoted rule.

redCorner.definition: highest lineup-warning tertile + lowest consensus-score tertile

comparisonCorner.definition: lowest lineup-warning tertile + highest consensus-score tertile

importantCounterexample.cell: highest lineup-warning tertile + highest consensus-score tertile

lineupWarningByConsensusGeometry.interpretation: Opponent lineup closeness was dangerous mainly when model conviction was also low; however the red-corner separation vanished in 2025 and the matrix is not monotonic, so it cannot be promoted as a live veto from V77.

premiumARouteFinding.interpretation: The Premium-A losses had a materially worse selected-side starter HR-risk advantage / more opponent-oriented HR-risk signal before the game. This is the strongest single route-specific opponent warning discovered in V77, but remains retrospective and adaptive.

aPlusRouteContext.interpretation: Only nine losses make inference sparse. Recent run-differential and bullpen warning showed large descriptive effects, but none survived the frozen 16-signal multiple-testing criteria.

scientificConclusion: The 138 historical losses do not share one universal rival trait. The largest 95-loss cluster is characterized more by cumulative opponent threat plus weaker model conviction than by one dominant signal. Premium-A losses show a separate starter-HR-risk warning. A+ losses are too sparse for stable inference. The next scientific step should freeze a small candidate warning architecture based on these route-specific mechanisms and validate it on fresh/unseen data; V77 itself must not alter live selection rules.
